**Proposed mechanism:** DPYS (HGNC:2879) —DISRUPTS→ Dihydropyrimidine (CHEBI:17035); Dihydropyrimidine (CHEBI:17035) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Dihydropyrimidine (CHEBI:17035) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Dihydropyrimidine (CHEBI:17035) —LEADS_TO→ Vomiting (HP:0011019); DPYS (HGNC:2879) —DISRUPTS→ Uracil (CHEBI:17794); Uracil (CHEBI:17794) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Mutations in DPYS can lead to reduced activity of dihydropyrimidinase, causing accumulation of dihydropyrimidines (MONDO:0013164) and potentially contributing to developmental delay and intellectual disability. In dihydropyrimidinuria (MONDO:0009111), a complete loss-of-function in DPYS leads to the accumulation of uracil and dihydropyrimidines, resulting in phenotypes like developmental delay and vomiting.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of developmental delay in patients with pathogenic variants in DPYS associated with dihydropyrimidine accumulation would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: gnomad v2.1.1 has no common variants in DPYS.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of DPYS in these conditions could inform therapeutic strategies targeting pyrimidine metabolism for both disorders.
